Subject: Silverpine edge inference discovery — technical follow-up

Hi Maria / Liam,

Thanks again for the time today — good discussion. Quick recap from our side so we have alignment before the deeper technical session: 

What we heard (key pain & goals)
- Unpredictable tail latency during daytime trading windows and batch reports (spikes up to ~800 RPS).
- Cold-start stalls when a model variant scales from 0 to burst capacity; customer-visible p95 spikes past 500ms.
- Desire to push inference nearer to edge gateways for market data enrichment (VPC peering to GCP us-east1).
- Regulatory requirement: logs/audit trail for inference requests (retention 2 years) and no model training on customer data.

SLOs you mentioned
- Target p50 ~20–30ms for small prompts (<=128 tokens), p95 <= 80ms; 99th percentile <= 150ms for peak traffic.
- Target throughput baseline ~200 RPS with bursts to 1k RPS for short windows.

Model & workload notes
- Primary model: open-weights Llama-derived 13B, exploring quantized 4-bit FPQ + mixed-precision for speed.
- Two classes of calls: short low-latency enrichment calls (50–150 tokens) and long-running summarization (>=1k tokens) where we can accept higher latency.

Topology constraints we heard
- GCP-only deployment preferred, but must support isolated VPC and customer-managed encryption keys (KMS).
- Prefer private deployment (VPC) for production, but open to Redwood Dedicated for early POC to validate latency/cost.

Next steps (proposed)
1) Technical deep-dive (deep topology + perf knobs) — 90 minutes with infra + ML engineer — propose Tue 10th or Wed 11th (I’ll send calendar invites).
2) Redwood to sketch two deployment options: (A) Dedicated pool with prefix caching and warm-warm sizing; (B) Private VPC deployment with autoscaling + standby warm nodes.
3) Draft mutual action plan & cost sketch for initial 3-month POC.

I attached a short action-plan template and a sketch we will fill during the deep-dive. If anything above is off, call it out — otherwise we’ll lock the deep-dive slot.

Thanks,
Priyom
Principal Solutions Engineer
Redwood Inference

Thanks, Priyom — this is a good capture. A couple clarifications from our side: 

- The p95 <= 80ms target is for the enrichment calls only; for summarization we’re fine with p95 up to 1.5s.
- Bursts tend to be short (30–90s) but frequent during market opens; we need autoscaling that doesn’t cause cold-start spikes.
- We run sensitive customer identifiers in a separate tenant; for the POC we can use anonymized traffic but logs/audit must be production-ready.

A few asks ahead of the deep-dive: 
- Can Redwood outline expected warm vs cold cost delta for a 13B quantized profile (ballpark $/hour)?
- Is there an option to route enrichment calls to a smaller 7B quantized variant for cheaper low-latency inference, fallback to 13B for summaries?

I’ll loop procurement once we have a POC plan. Wed 11th works better for our infra lead (11:00–12:30 PT).

–Maria

Hi Maria — thanks for the extra color. A few technical notes ahead of Wed: 

1) Mixed model routing: yes, we can do a primary routing policy that sends short enrichment prompts to a 7B quantized variant and long requests to 13B. Redwood supports per-route model pinning + automatic fallback on error or when capacity-constrained.

2) Warm vs cold cost: rough estimates (very approximate):
   - 13B quantized (4-bit FPQ) on dedicated T4/RTX-class equivalent: warm node ~ $1.80/hr; cold (spin-up + cold-cache) effective cost higher during bursts.
   - 7B quantized: ~ $0.65–0.90/hr warm.
   - For short spikes we recommend keeping a small pool of warm standby workers + predictive prefix caching for the most common enrichment prefixes (reduces token compute by ~30–50%).

3) Autoscaling topology options to review on Wed: 
   - Option A (Dedicated POC): Reserved Dedicated pool in us-east1, configure burst capacity and standby warm nodes. Fastest to validate perf; minimal infra changes on your side.
   - Option B (Private VPC): Deploy Redwood Private control plane in your GCP project (VPC peering). Adds networking configuration and KMS setup; better long-term isolation.

4) Observability & audit: Redwood can stream structured logs to your GCS or BigQuery with per-request metadata (request id, model version, token counts). Retention/exports can satisfy the 2-year requirement.

I’ll bring a short runbook for prefix caching, suggested batching windows (target batch latency 5–12ms), and fallback routing to the deep-dive.

-karthik
